title: US navy sailor jumps overboard after 250 days at sea
excerpt: Military families warn that 5,000 onboard aircraft carrier have reached breaking point as Iran war drags on
content_html:
Military families warn that 5,000 onboard aircraft carrier have reached breaking point as Iran war drags on

Emily Smith Foreign Breaking News Reporter Show biography

Emily covers breaking news from all over the world. She previously reported on home news and politics for The Telegraph. You can reach her at emily.smith@telegraph.co.uk

Published 13 August 2026 9:59am BST

A sailor jumped from the USS Abraham Lincoln as a mental health crisis engulfed the aircraft carrier during its ninth month at sea.

The carrier, sent to the Middle East in January, has reached a record deployment of 265 days while supporting American forces during the Iran War.

The sailor was quickly rescued and medically evacuated after seemingly attempting to end their life, according to CNN. It is unclear whether they have returned to duty.

Military families say the 5,000-strong crew has reached breaking point, with some attempting to jump overboard in an attempt to end their lives as the war drags on.

There have been complaints about lavatories, showers, food and burnout from sailors onboard the warship who have not stepped on dry land this year.

The US is preparing to send the USS George Washington, another Nimitz-class carrier, to replace the Lincoln, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The USS George Washington is based in Japan and has been operating in the Pacific in recent weeks. US officials said its deployment to the Middle East was part of a previously scheduled rotation plan.

Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, said reports about poor conditions were “completely misrepresented”.

“We make sure every ‌ship, ‌every ⁠crew, every captain has everything we can provide them ⁠at every single moment. Some deployments are longer than others, and ‌I have more respect and gratitude for those sailors ‌than anybody. What ⁠they do in those high ⁠seas in those austere conditions with less port calls – it’s incredible,” ‌he told reporters during a ⁠visit ⁠to Panama.

The Lincoln departed San Diego in California on Nov 21, 2025 for duty in the South China Sea before being rerouted to the Middle East ahead of Operation Epic Fury in February.

The deployment was expected to end in May but has been extended without a return date.

Food shortages and broken plumbing are among the long list of issues on the ship, which has prompted calls from Congress members to take action.

Annabelle Loma, the wife of a sailor serving on the ship, told the Military Times that her husband was now on medical hold after trying to jump from the carrier.

“He’s scared,” Ms Loma said. “He thinks he’ll get a dishonourable discharge and, just because he was burnt out, his 13-year career is ruined, just like that.”

Maria Rodriguez said that her husband prevented another sailor from jumping overboard, thwarting a suicide attempt.

Another spouse, one of 200 who met navy leaders in San Diego to discuss the concerns, said her husband had texted her saying “he hopes he doesn’t wake up tomorrow”.

In April, there was widespread criticism after photos emerged of poor-quality and rationed food on the ship.

One meal consisted of what appeared to be a pre-cooked gyros slice, a pile of an unidentifiable brown substance and some boiled carrots.

Iran was quick to mock the US over the food. The Iranian embassy in Tunisia wrote on X: “OMG unbelievable!! This is what Trump is feeding his soldiers to open the Strait of Hormuz.”

Beyond the poor quality of meals, sailors are also facing shortages of basic items like milk, as supply runs are unable to deliver fresh food before it spoils.

In a text conversation shared with MeidasTouch, one sailor described the reality of the conditions, sharing a photo of cereal without milk: “Hey honey, I’m eating cereal rn. Wish there was milk, though. Haven’t had milk in three months.”

When asked why milk was unavailable, the sailor explained that supply chains cannot keep perishables fresh long enough for transit, noting that food often arrives rotten.

“This deployment is the worst one, and I pray no other boat goes through the same,” they added.

“The Navy does not care. The mission will always come first.”

‘Environment ripe for accidents’

There are also concerns about long workdays with no breaks in a dangerous environment.

Brett Snow, a navy veteran whose son is serving on the Lincoln, said: “It’s the most dangerous place in the world already, and now you’re grinding it out, day in and day out, with no breaks. It’s an environment that’s ripe for accidents.”

In a letter to Mr Hegseth, Senator Richard Blumenthal called for the navy to account for conditions aboard the aircraft carrier.

He voiced concern over “widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns” and other problems aboard the Lincoln.

Senator Ruben Gallego called for “an official oversight visit with the bipartisan senate delegation to the Lincoln to investigate the reported alarming conditions”.

“The way [Donald Trump] is treating our service members as he carries out this illegal war is not just disgusting, it’s dangerous,” he said.

Cdr Joseph Hontz, spokesman for the navy’s 5th Fleet, previously acknowledged that the deployment was challenging.

“Though more than 250 days on deployment is challenging for the crew and their equipment, they remain resilient and ready to accomplish any tasking given to them,” he said. “The ship remains fully capable of meeting all mission tasking.”

The US navy has been contacted for comment.

content_html_zh:
军人家属警告称，随着伊朗战争的持续，航母上的5000人已达到崩溃边缘

艾米丽·史密斯 (Emily Smith) 外国突发新闻记者秀传记 艾米丽 (Emily Smith) 报道来自世界各地的突发新闻。 她此前曾为《电讯报》报道过家庭新闻和政治。 您可以通过 emily.smith@telegraph.co.uk 联系她

发布于 2026 年 8 月 13 日上午 9:59（英国夏令时）

亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰在海上航行第九个月，精神健康危机席卷了这艘航空母舰，一名水手从这艘航空母舰上跳下。

这艘航母于 1 月份被派往中东，在伊朗战争期间为美军提供支援，部署时间达到了 265 天，创下了纪录。

据美国有线电视新闻网报道，这名水手似乎试图结束自己的生命，但很快就被救起并接受医疗后送。 目前尚不清楚他们是否已经返回岗位。

军人家属表示，随着战争的持续，5000 名船员已经达到了崩溃的边缘，一些人试图跳海结束自己的生命。

今年还没有踏上陆地的军舰上的水手们抱怨厕所、淋浴、食物和倦怠。

据《华尔街日报》报道，美国正准备派遣另一艘尼米兹级航母乔治·华盛顿号来取代林肯号。

乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰以日本为基地，最近几周一直在太平洋执行任务。 美国官员表示，其向中东的部署是先前安排的轮换计划的一部分。

美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth) 表示，有关恶劣条件的报道“完全被歪曲”。

“我们确保每艘船、每名船员、每名船长每时每刻都拥有我们可以提供的一切。 有些部署比其他部署时间更长，我对这些水手比任何人都更加尊重和感激。 他们在公海条件恶劣、港口停靠次数较少的情况下所做的事情令人难以置信，”他在访问巴拿马期间告诉记者。

林肯号于 2025 年 11 月 21 日从加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥出发前往南中国海执行任务，然后在 2 月份的史诗愤怒行动之前改道前往中东。

部署预计将于五月结束，但已延长，但没有返回日期。

食物短缺和管道破损是船上的一长串问题之一，这促使国会议员呼吁采取行动。

在船上服役的一名水手的妻子安娜贝尔·洛马告诉《军事时报》，她的丈夫在试图从航母上跳下后目前处于医疗留置状态。

“他很害怕，”洛马女士说。 “他认为自己会被不光彩地开除，仅仅因为他精疲力竭，他 13 年的职业生涯就毁了，就这样。”

玛丽亚·罗德里格斯说，她的丈夫阻止了另一名水手跳海，阻止了一次自杀企图。

另一位配偶是在圣地亚哥会见海军领导人讨论这些问题的 200 人之一，她说她的丈夫给她发短信说“他希望明天不要醒来”。

4月份，船上食品质量低劣且实行定量配给的照片曝光后，引起了广泛的批评。

其中一顿饭似乎包括一块预先煮熟的陀螺片、一堆无法辨认的棕色物质和一些煮熟的胡萝卜。

伊朗很快就食品问题嘲笑美国。 伊朗驻突尼斯大使馆在X上写道：“天哪，难以置信！！ 这就是特朗普为打开霍尔木兹海峡而向其士兵提供的食物。”

除了膳食质量差之外，水手们还面临牛奶等基本物品的短缺，因为供应无法在新鲜食物变质之前提供。

在与 MeidasTouch 分享的文字对话中，一名水手描述了现实情况，并分享了一张没有牛奶的麦片照片：“嘿，亲爱的，我正在吃麦片。 但还是希望有牛奶。 三个月没喝奶了。”

当被问及为什么没有牛奶时，该水手解释说，供应链无法在运输过程中保持易腐烂食品足够长的新鲜度，并指出食物到达时经常会腐烂。

他们补充说：“这次部署是最糟糕的一次，我祈祷没有其他船只经历同样的情况。”

“海军不在乎。 使命永远是第一位的。”

“环境容易发生事故”

人们还担心在危险的环境中长时间工作而没有休息。

海军退伍军人布雷特·斯诺（Brett Snow）的儿子在林肯号上服役，他说：“这里已经是世界上最危险的地方了，现在你要日复一日地艰苦奋斗，没有休息。 这是一个容易发生事故的环境。”

参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔在给赫格斯先生的一封信中呼吁海军考虑航空母舰上的情况。

他对“广泛报道的基本物资短缺、水污染、管道问题、心理健康恶化、甲板安全问题”以及林肯号上的其他问题表示担忧。

参议员鲁本·加列戈呼吁“两党参议院代表团对林肯号进行正式监督访问，以调查报告的令人震惊的情况”。

“（唐纳德·特朗普）在进行这场非法战争时对待我们军人的方式不仅令人厌恶，而且很危险，”他说。

海军第五舰队发言人约瑟夫·洪茨中校此前承认，部署具有挑战性。

他说：“虽然超过 250 天的部署对机组人员及其设备来说是一个挑战，但他们仍然保持弹性并准备好完成交给他们的任何任务。” “这艘船仍然完全有能力完成所有任务。”

已联系美国海军请其置评。
